SELECT renewables_share_elec FROM energy WHERE country = 'Israel' AND year = 2025

claims.quote: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity

claims.note: data says 3.41, report says 14.3; also inconsistent: shares for Israel 2025 add up to more than 100%: 16.9 (renewables_share_elec) + 79.7 (gas_share_elec) + 14.3 (coal_share_elec)

requirements.evidence: Renewables rose by 15% between 2015 and 2025, reaching 16.9% of Israel's electricity.
requirements.reason: The report provides both the 2025 renewables share and the change since 2015.

requirements.evidence: In 2025 coal still provided 14.3% of Israel's electricity, so the phase-out is far from complete.
requirements.reason: The status of coal in Israel's electricity mix for 2025 is explicitly stated.
The report does not compare Israel with any Mediterranean peers.

requirements.evidence: Total generation increased from 64.2 TWh to 82.1 TWh over the decade.
requirements.reason: The exact growth of Israel's total electricity generation between 2015 and 2025 is provided.

requirements.evidence: Israel's reliance on gas (79.7% of generation in 2025) is the main vulnerability: any disruption to gas supply would hit most of the power system.
requirements.reason: A key risk grounded in the data regarding gas reliance is clearly identified.
